correctness.rationale: For each unit state both coefficient-energy densities a_f,b_f are measurable, nonnegative and integrate to one. The measurable selection σ={a_f≤b_f} attains the min density for that state and the opposite selection the max. Their integrals equal 1 ∓ (1/2)∫|a_f-b_f|. Commuting the joint infimum and joint supremum over f and measurable σ yields exact optimal universal bounds 1−τ and 1+τ; the same partition need NOT optimize every state. Partial positive frame operators exist by bounded Parseval forms. D_σ=S1,σ−S2,σ is self-adjoint, and sup_σ||D_σ||=sup_f(1/2)∫|a_f-b_f| because the signed density has total zero. Two-atom operators A1=P1,A2=P2,B1=(1−t)P1+tP2,B2=tP1+(1−t)P2 form legitimate Parseval systems and give τ=t, mixed eigenvalues 1±t even t=0 and t=1. Infinite-dimensional statement does not assert attainment of τ.
residual_risks: Measurability of local densities and weak operator integrability explicitly assumed; none is inferred from an arbitrary nonmeasurable family.

originality.rationale: The exact Parseval quantitative invariant is an operational characterization by worst-state total variation and partial-operator norm. Foundational weaving theory proves weak/strong equivalence and sufficient perturbations; generalized g-frame theory supplies extremal bounds relative to individual frame bounds, not this exact formula. A two-atom continuous threshold family makes its sharpness substantive. The Ghosh–Samanta theorem has a pointwise/local positivity ambiguity and is not asserted refuted under its stronger reading.
residual_risks: Operator-valued measure and POVM discrimination literature might formulate the identical Parseval overlap result in probabilistic language without weaving terminology.
Novelty is the exact characterization/sharpness, not the elementary L1 minimum identity itself.

value.rationale: It converts all measurable allocation patterns into a single exact worst-state distance, determining the precise lower and upper universal stability constants even for non-atomic continuous systems. The sharp two-atom continuum and t=1 failure with two identical global frame operators show why global equalities alone are insufficient. This is a motivated exact robustness theorem, not a self-contained but arbitrary algebra trick.
residual_risks: Computing the sup over states may itself be difficult in infinite dimensions.

limitations: Only two Parseval sources with measurable unit-vector energy densities; unequal-frame Parseval normalization and m>2 weavings not covered.
Source Theorem 2.15 interpretation is conditional; no unconditional published-error claim.
